Triage: lands in `domain:devx` (`content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` + `scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`); rationale: class (b) on the **over-claim**, ⛔ not on the omission.

⚠️ On its face this is a docs omission — three gates unlisted — and 「漏列成员不是 (a)」 would close it. ⭐ **What admits it is the pin**: `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` already contains exactly the assertion this needs — *"names every first-party command the job actually runs"* plus its inverse *"credits no job with a first-party command it does not run"* — and it is scoped to **one workflow**:

```ts
describe('ci-cd-pipeline.md — ci.yml job table', () => {
  const ciWorkflow = fs.readFileSync(path.join(workflowDir, 'ci.yml'), 'utf8');
```

`lint.yml` is covered only by the workflow-**inventory** pin, which requires a heading naming the file and nothing about its contents. ⇒ **`lint.yml` has a heading, so it passes while its step list drifts.** A green that asserts the page is reconciled against the workflows, while being structurally blind to this one. `Bug`.

⭐ The measurement carries its own positive control — the same scan, same parser, same section text reports `check-lint-coverage.mjs`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm check` as **PRESENT**. ⇒ The three zeros are readings, not a broken matcher.

`priority:p3`: contributor-facing docs, no runtime effect. ⚠️ The direction is the bad one — the page **understates** the gate, so a contributor reading it to find out why `Lint` is red will not find `check-entry-guard` or `check-upstream-port-parity` there at all — but the failure is recoverable in seconds by reading the workflow.

⛔ **Do not fix the prose alone.** That repeats the drift, and the test file this page depends on records that lesson at length for this same page. ⇒ Either extend the existing both-directions command pin to `lint.yml` (a section-scoped command set on both sides — the job is a single `lint` job, so it needs no job-table parse) or move `lint.yml`'s steps into a pinned table the way `ci.yml`'s are.

⚠️ Two live neighbours on the same page, ⛔ neither a duplicate and ⛔ neither to be folded in: objectui#8006 (the `check-skills-paths.mjs` description) and objectui#7965 (three drifted live counts). ⚠️ And whoever lands objectui#7692's fourth step should update the section in the same PR, or this card reopens with a fourth gate.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.

**The serial chain that held this card has cleared.** #8015 was queued behind #8006 on this document; **PR #8417 merged at 21:31:28Z as `a7c5ac399`**, so this card is now the head and branches from the post-merge `main`. ⛔ It does not race that change — the sentence #8006 fixed (the Skill Guide Paths scan roots, now naming both `skills/` and `.claude/skills/`) is settled and out of scope here.

⭐ **#8006's dev handed this card its strongest evidence, unasked.** Verifying that no pin covered *its* sentence, it replaced that sentence with an obvious falsehood and re-ran the eleven test files that read this document: **11/11 files, 404/404 tests still green**, `check-doc-links` still exit 0. That is a live demonstration of the very gap this card names — `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` scopes its "names every first-party command the job actually runs" assertion (and its inverse) to `ci.yml` alone, so `lint.yml` passes on the workflow-INVENTORY pin — a heading exists — while its step list drifts.

⇒ This card is therefore **not** a prose card. Its centre is the pin's scope; the three undescribed gates (`check-entry-guard.mjs`, `check-upstream-port-parity.mjs`, `check-cross-repo-closer-outcome.mjs`) are the symptom that scope permits.

⚠️ Two coordinates on this card must be re-derived, not trusted: it was measured on `28cfff4`, and #8006 showed this document's line numbers had already drifted twice (551→574, 581→599). The **set** of commands `lint.yml` runs is the reading that matters, taken from the workflow on today's tree.

Race re-read at 21:56Z: one `Claim:`, `5575965569`.

**The brief puts the pin at the centre, not the three bullets.** `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` already carries the right assertion in both directions — every command the job runs is named, and no command is credited that it does not run — scoped to **`ci.yml` alone**. `lint.yml` passes on the workflow-INVENTORY pin (a heading exists) while its step list drifts, which is how three blocking gates went undescribed. ⇒ The dev generalises the assertion; the bullets follow from it.

⭐ **The evidence was produced yesterday by #8006's dev, unasked**: replacing that card's sentence with an obvious falsehood left **11/11 files and 404/404 tests green** and `check-doc-links` at exit 0. Nothing looks at this page's contents beyond the `ci.yml` table.

⛔ Re-derivation demanded, ⛔ not the card's `28cfff4` list and ⛔ no line numbers — this document's coordinates drifted twice in the last card (551→574, 581→599). A **positive control** for the parser is required so a zero is not read off a broken matcher, and **both** ablation directions must be shown with on-disk proof before any result is read.
